newsitem.title: USA: Duff & Phelps reaffirms IBM debt ratings.
newsitem.headline: Duff & Phelps reaffirms IBM debt ratings.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Thursday it reaffirmed the senior debt rating of International Business Machines Corp and its subsidiaries at Single A Plus, the preferred stock rating at Single A and the commercial paper rating at D One.

With 1996 revenues of $76 billion, IBM is a leader in most egments of the information technology industry, said Duff & Phelps. The company generates significant excess cash flow to fund internal growth, acquisitions and share repurchases.

While the company's net income was down slightly last year, there were positive indications from a credit sense in terms of IBM's ability to maintain profitability at a realtively stable level, Duff & Phelps said.

A sharp decline in semiconductor memory prices, negative currency trends and a weak European market were offset by strong performance in personal computers, continued cost-cutting efforts and other positive factors.

Duff & Phelps said its rating also recognizes the likelihood of continued adverse industry conditions in which higher-margin proprietary mainframe computer systems with related software and maintenance revenue streams are displaced by smaller, standardized and more competitive lower-margin systems.
